S.FORM: tee=pa=ku=kani sii sua siŋsi=maku ia, tee=kani taavalaʔə sua makai isi=mita miana ma-maraŋ, miana ʔaisi=pa ma-maraŋ=mita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: teepakukani ʂii sua ʂiŋʂimaku ia teekani taavaɾaʔə sua makai iʂimita miana mamaraŋ miana ʔaiʂipa mamaraŋmita kanakanavu
S.FORM: teepakukani sii sua singsimaku ia, teekani taavara'e sua makai isimita miana mamarang, miana 'aisipa mamarangmita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: teepakukani ʂii sua ʂiŋʂimaku ia teekani taava[r|ɾ]aʔe sua makai iʂimita miana mama[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ʔaiʂipa mama[r|ɾ]aŋmita kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: I will tell my teacher about the taboo in the past that I know about. This was when the Kanakanavu elders were still alive.

S.FORM: sua pu-a-iisua karianumai=kani ia, sii-paka-siin=naku miəra.
S.PHON: sua puaiisua karianumaikani ia ʂiipakaʂiinnaku miəra
S.FORM: sua puaiisua karianumaikani ia, siipakasiinnaku miera.
S.PHON: sua puaiisua ka[r|ɾ]ianumaikani ia ʂiipakaʂiinnaku mie[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: I talked about pangolin yesterday.

S.FORM: "vanai=kimi kanakanavu kaʔan paa-ʔupa-ʔupaŋ c<um>əʔəra ʔinia ŋuai=pa sua ni-pa-pa-cəvərə kimia kanakanavu," kisa-ən=naku
S.PHON: vanaikimi kanakanavu kaʔan paaʔupaʔupaŋ ʦuməʔəra ʔinia ŋuaipa sua nipapaʦəvərə kimia kanakanavu kisaənnaku
S.FORM: "vanaikimi kanakanavu ka'an paa'upa'upang c<um>e'era 'inia nguaipa sua nipapacevere kimia kanakanavu," kisaennaku
S.PHON: vanaikimi kanakanavu kaʔan paaʔupaʔupaŋ ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]a ʔinia ŋuaipa sua nipapaʦeve[r|ɾ]e kimia kanakanavu kisaennaku
S.TRANSL: "The reason we don't harass a pangolin when we see it is that once it kept a Kanakanavu person alive," I said.

S.FORM: a-paica-u=pa sian pu-kari-kari misa.
S.PHON: apaiʦaupa ʂian pukarikari misa
S.FORM: apaicaupa sian pukarikari misa.
S.PHON: apaiʦaupa ʂian puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i misa
S.TRANSL: He wants me to tell a story (about pangolins)(by a tape recorder).

S.FORM: nain sua ŋacaʔ-in misai? tee=maku puu-kari-kari-in makasii.
S.PHON: nain sua ŋaʦaʔin misai teemaku puukarikariin makaʂii
S.FORM: nain sua ngaca'in misai? teemaku puukarikariin makasii.
S.PHON: nain sua ŋaʦaʔin misai teemaku puuka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]iin makaʂii
S.TRANSL: On what basis can I tell it? I shall tell it now.

S.FORM: naini vanai=ta kaʔan tia=t<um>a-tani-ulaʔə sua karianumai.
S.PHON: naini vanaita kaʔan tiatumataniuɾaʔə sua karianumai
S.FORM: naini vanaita ka'an tiat<um>ataniura'e sua karianumai.
S.PHON: naini vanaita kaʔan tiatumataniu[r|ɾ]aʔe sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai
S.TRANSL: What reason is there for us not to abuse a pangolin?

S.FORM: sua karianumai miana ia, ma-kaasi sua ŋacaʔ-in ʔuuna=kani iikita kanakanavu miana.
S.PHON: sua karianumai miana ia makaaʂi sua ŋaʦaʔin ʔuunakani iikita kanakanavu miana
S.FORM: sua karianumai miana ia, makaasi sua ngaca'in 'uunakani iikita kanakanavu miana.
S.PHON: sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai miana ia makaaʂi sua ŋaʦaʔin ʔuunakani iikita kanakanavu miana
S.TRANSL: The pangolin in the past was like this in our Kanakanavu tradition.

S.FORM: makai tia=naaʔu=kara sa ʔuusu=kara?
S.PHON: makai tianaaʔukara sa ʔuusukara
S.FORM: makai tianaa'ukara sa 'uusukara?
S.PHON: makai tianaaʔuka[r|ɾ]a sa ʔuusuka[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Is her name Naa'u or 'Uusu?

S.FORM: t<um>imana=ku kaari ia, ma-maaraŋ miana ia, makai tia=ʔuusu misai.
S.PHON: tumimanaku kaari ia mamaaraŋ miana ia makai tiaʔuusu misai
S.FORM: t<um>imanaku kaari ia, mamaarang miana ia, makai tia'uusu misai.
S.PHON: tumimanaku kaa[r|ɾ]i ia mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia makai tiaʔuusu misai
S.TRANSL: As I learned from the elders in the past, it was 'Uusu.

S.FORM: ni-ara-aka ni-ara-aka=cu sua iikita ma-maaraŋ miana ia, kaʔan makai mamisa puuʔa=cu haaku.
S.PHON: niaraaka niaraakaʦu sua iikita mamaaraŋ miana ia kaʔan makai mamisa puuʔaʦu haaku
S.FORM: niaraaka niaraakacu sua iikita mamaarang miana ia, ka'an makai mamisa puu'acu haaku.
S.PHON: nia[r|ɾ]aaka nia[r|ɾ]aakaʦu sua iikita mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia kaʔan makai mamisa puuʔaʦu haaku
S.TRANSL: In the past, when an elder passed away, people could not afford a coffin, as now.

S.FORM: iikita miana ia, kaa-manəŋ=kita maamia ni-arəara m-ari-cəkəcəkə.
S.PHON: iikita miana ia kaamanəŋkita maamia niarəara mariʦəkəʦəkə
S.FORM: iikita miana ia, kaamanengkita maamia niareara maricekeceke.
S.PHON: iikita miana ia kaamaneŋkita maamia nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a ma[r|ɾ]iʦekeʦeke
S.TRANSL: In the past, we just assembled pieces of board (into a coffin) by nailing them together.

S.FORM: makasua=kita kanakanavu miana. pakisia ka-vaŋvaŋ ia, makasua sumukun ka-vaŋəvaŋə ia, maka-sua.
S.PHON: makasuakita kanakanavu miana pakiʂia kavaŋvaŋ ia makasua sumukun kavaŋəvaŋə ia makasua
S.FORM: makasuakita kanakanavu miana. pakisia kavangvang ia, makasua sumukun kavangevange ia, makasua.
S.PHON: makasuakita kanakanavu miana pakiʂia kavaŋvaŋ ia makasua sumukun kavaŋevaŋe ia makasua
S.TRANSL: In the past, we Kanakanavu did that. All the Chinese and Bunun also did that.

S.FORM: ʔakia=pa mia-iisua makai puuʔa satuʔu misai
S.PHON: ʔakiapa miaiisua makai puuʔa satuʔu misai
S.FORM: 'akiapa miaiisua makai puu'a satu'u misai
S.PHON: ʔakiapa miaiisua makai puuʔa satuʔu misai
S.TRANSL: It is said that there was no coffin yet at that time.

S.FORM: sua mia-iisua ia, ʔuuna=kani ni-ara-aka kanakanavu. naaʔu=kani ŋanai-ni ni-ara-aka ni-isəʔ-an=cu=kani.
S.PHON: sua miaiisua ia ʔuunakani niaraaka kanakanavu naaʔukani ŋanaini niaraaka niisəʔanʦukani
S.FORM: sua miaiisua ia, 'uunakani niaraaka kanakanavu. naa'ukani nganaini niaraaka niise'ancukani.
S.PHON: sua miaiisua ia ʔuunakani nia[r|ɾ]aaka kanakanavu naaʔukani ŋanaini nia[r|ɾ]aaka niiseʔanʦukani
S.TRANSL: At that time, a certain Kanakanavu person died. Her name was said to be Naa'u who died and who was put (into a coffin).

S.FORM: avic-ai=cu t<um>acucu ʔ<um>avunu.
S.PHON: aviʦaiʦu tumaʦuʦu ʔumavunu
S.FORM: avicaicu t<um>acucu '<um>avunu.
S.PHON: aviʦaiʦu tumaʦuʦu ʔumavunu
S.TRANSL: She was taken to be buried.

S.FORM: ʔ<um>avun ma-naasə ni-a-pitu=cu taniaara t<in>acuc-a ʔinia ni-ʔavun-a ʔinia.
S.PHON: ʔumavun manaasə niapituʦu taniaara tinaʦuʦa ʔinia niʔavuna ʔinia
S.FORM: '<um>avun manaase niapitucu taniaara t<in>acuca 'inia ni'avuna 'inia.
S.PHON: ʔumavun manaase niapituʦu taniaa[r|ɾ]a tinaʦuʦa ʔinia niʔavuna ʔinia
S.TRANSL: Seven days later, she was taken to be buried.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makaasua ni-araanai=ʔai naanu sua karianumai kaur-ai=kani ʔinia iisua.
S.PHON: makaasua niaraanaiʔai naanu sua karianumai kauraikani ʔinia iisua
S.FORM: makaasua niaraanai'ai naanu sua karianumai kauraikani 'inia iisua.
S.PHON: makaasua nia[r|ɾ]aanaiʔai naanu sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai kau[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia iisua
S.TRANSL: Somehow a pangolin came over to dig up where (she was buried).

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makaasua ni-araanai=ʔai kusa naanu sua karianumai kaur-ai=kani ʔinia iisua.
S.PHON: makaasua niaraanaiʔai kusa naanu sua karianumai kauraikani ʔinia iisua
S.FORM: makaasua niaraanai'ai kusa naanu sua karianumai kauraikani 'inia iisua.
S.PHON: makaasua nia[r|ɾ]aanaiʔai kusa naanu sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai kau[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia iisua
S.TRANSL: Somehow a pangolin came over to dig up where (she was buried).

S.FORM: kisa-i=naku sua misaini=ʔai taavalaʔ-ən=kiai na=mu-liuŋ ni-arəara ni-ʔavun-a ʔinia
S.PHON: kisainaku sua misainiʔai taavaɾaʔənkiai namuɾiuŋ niarəara niʔavuna ʔinia
S.FORM: kisainaku sua misaini'ai taavara'enkiai namuriung niareara ni'avuna 'inia
S.PHON: kisainaku sua misainiʔai taava[r|ɾ]aʔenkiai namu[r|ɾ]iuŋ nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a niʔavuna ʔinia
S.TRANSL: I wonder how it came to know (where to dig) around the coffin.

S.FORM: u-kusa-i=kani sua karianumai k<um>auru ka-vaŋvaŋ ki-ləkə-ləkə mata-lava ni-arəara ni-paica-a ni-ʔavun-a
S.PHON: ukusaikani sua karianumai kumauru kavaŋvaŋ kiɾəkəɾəkə mataɾava niarəara nipaiʦaa niʔavuna
S.FORM: ukusaikani sua karianumai k<um>auru kavangvang kirekereke matarava niareara nipaicaa ni'avuna
S.PHON: ukusaikani sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai kumau[r|ɾ]u kavaŋvaŋ ki[r|ɾ]eke[r|ɾ]eke mata[r|ɾ]ava nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a nipaiʦaa niʔavuna
S.TRANSL: caau iisua. person that The pangolin dug up all around the coffin where the dead person was buried.

S.FORM: ku-rupaŋ-ai=kani ʔinia k<um>auru, paki-tutui=kani ʔinia sua ni-arəara.
S.PHON: kurupaŋaikani ʔinia kumauru pakitutuikani ʔinia sua niarəara
S.FORM: kurupangaikani 'inia k<um>auru, pakitutuikani 'inia sua niareara.
S.PHON: ku[r|ɾ]upaŋaikani ʔinia kumau[r|ɾ]u pakitutuikani ʔinia sua nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Having dug it up, (the pangolin) tried to uncover the coffin in the same way as a wild pig with its nose.

S.FORM: paki-tutui=kani ʔinia sua ni-arəara, ara-takarə=kani sua ni-arəara, ara-ʔənəvə.
S.PHON: pakitutuikani ʔinia sua niarəara aratakarəkani sua niarəara araʔənəvə
S.FORM: pakitutuikani 'inia sua niareara, aratakarekani sua niareara, ara'eneve.
S.PHON: pakitutuikani ʔinia sua nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a a[r|ɾ]ataka[r|ɾ]ekani sua nia[r|ɾ]ea[r|ɾ]a a[r|ɾ]aʔeneve
S.TRANSL: It opened the coffin by pushing the lid to the side, as a wild pig would.

S.FORM: ma-kaasi sua ni-muʔun ʔinia ni-ara-aka caau ia, putu-ʔənəv-ai=kani karianumai si-ʔinəv-ai-ni.
S.PHON: makaaʂi sua nimuʔun ʔinia niaraaka ʦaau ia putuʔənəvaikani karianumai ʂiʔinəvaini
S.FORM: makaasi sua nimu'un 'inia niaraaka caau ia, putu'enevaikani karianumai si'inevaini.
S.PHON: makaaʂi sua nimuʔun ʔinia nia[r|ɾ]aaka ʦaau ia putuʔenevaikani ka[r|ɾ]ianumai ʂiʔinevaini
S.TRANSL: It revived the dead in the coffin when the pangolin opened it.

S.FORM: ara-takarə=kan sua ni-ʔavun-a ʔinia kanakanavu.
S.PHON: aratakarəkan sua niʔavuna ʔinia kanakanavu
S.FORM: aratakarekan sua ni'avuna 'inia kanakanavu.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]ataka[r|ɾ]ekan sua niʔavuna ʔinia kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: The buried dead person was now standing up.

S.FORM: "aaʔa, aaman=pa=kasu culu, iivaa=kasu m-ari-pa-piniŋ=pa ʔikua," misa=kani nanakə iisua.
S.PHON: aaʔa aamanpakasu ʦuɾu iivaakasu maripapiniŋpa ʔikua misakani nanakə iisua
S.FORM: "aa'a, aamanpakasu curu, iivaakasu maripapiningpa 'ikua," misakani nanake iisua.
S.PHON: aaʔa aamanpakasu ʦu[r|ɾ]u iivaakasu ma[r|ɾ]ipapiniŋpa ʔikua misakani nanake iisua
S.TRANSL: "Ah, fortunately, it is you who took me out," said the woman.

S.FORM: "makasua=cu ma-manəŋ si kaʔan=cu=kasu tia=tani-ulaʔə. iivaa=kasu a-pa-cəvərə kimia," misa=kani nanakə iisua.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mamanəŋ ʂi kaʔanʦukasu tiataniuɾaʔə iivaakasu apaʦəvərə kimia misakani nanakə iisua
S.FORM: "makasuacu mamaneng si ka'ancukasu tiataniura'e. iivaakasu apacevere kimia," misakani nanake iisua.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mamaneŋ ʂi kaʔanʦukasu tiataniu[r|ɾ]aʔe iivaakasu apaʦeve[r|ɾ]e kimia misakani nanake iisua
S.TRANSL: "You are so nice that you won't be abused from now on. You are the only one (pangolin) who could revive us," said the woman.

S.FORM: araanai=cu ʔinia sua iikita kanakanavu sua karianumai ia, kaʔan taavalaʔə t<um>ani-ulaʔə.
S.PHON: araanaiʦu ʔinia sua iikita kanakanavu sua karianumai ia kaʔan taavaɾaʔə tumaniuɾaʔə
S.FORM: araanaicu 'inia sua iikita kanakanavu sua karianumai ia, ka'an taavara'e t<um>aniura'e.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aanaiʦu ʔinia sua iikita kanakanavu sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai ia kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔe tumaniu[r|ɾ]aʔe
S.TRANSL: We Kanakanavu people have not been able to abuse pangolins ever since.

S.FORM: ʔapacuʔ-ai ma-maaraŋ miana ia, r<um>a-riŋai, puu-riŋai-n karianumai ia, ʔeesi=pa ʔinia putu-kia-kiau ia, ma-ala=kia ranəŋ ʔuici, s<um>aʔəmə puruu-muŋ na ʔacipi karianumai ni-pati-kusa talisi.
S.PHON: ʔapaʦuʔai mamaaraŋ miana ia rumariŋai puuriŋain karianumai ia ʔeeʂipa ʔinia putukiakiau ia maaɾakia ranəŋ ʔuitʂi sumaʔəmə puruumuŋ na ʔatʂipi karianumai nipatikusa taɾiʂi
S.FORM: 'apacu'ai mamaarang miana ia, r<um>aringai, puuringain karianumai ia, 'eesipa 'inia putukiakiau ia, maarakia raneng 'uici, s<um>a'eme puruumung na 'acipi karianumai nipatikusa tarisi.
S.PHON: ʔapaʦuʔai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]iŋai puu[r|ɾ]iŋain ka[r|ɾ]ianumai ia ʔeeʂipa ʔinia putukiakiau ia maa[r|ɾ]akia [r|ɾ]aneŋ ʔuitʂi sumaʔeme pu[r|ɾ]uumuŋ na ʔatʂipi ka[r|ɾ]ianumai nipatikusa ta[r|ɾ]iʂi
S.TRANSL: Even when our Kanakanavu people in the past set up a trap, if a pangolin was trapped and if it was still alive, they would take a rattan leaf, chew it, and spit on the legs of the pangolin that was caught by the rope.

S.FORM: ni-pati-kusa talisi pa-li-aluma putu-uluŋu-un pa-li-aluma.
S.PHON: nipatikusa taɾiʂi paɾiaɾuma putuuɾuŋuun paɾiaɾuma
S.FORM: nipatikusa tarisi pariaruma putuurunguun pariaruma.
S.PHON: nipatikusa ta[r|ɾ]iʂi pa[r|ɾ]ia[r|ɾ]uma putuu[r|ɾ]uŋuun pa[r|ɾ]ia[r|ɾ]uma
S.TRANSL: They would untie the rope where it was hooked and release it.

S.FORM: kisa-i ma-maaraŋ miana ia, makaa-sua.
S.PHON: kisai mamaaraŋ miana ia makaasua
S.FORM: kisai mamaarang miana ia, makaasua.
S.PHON: kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia makaasua
S.TRANSL: Our elders in the past said so.

S.FORM: "kaʔan taavalaʔ-ən t<um>ani-ulaʔə sua karianumai ni-pa-pa-cəvərə kitana m-ari-takarə," misai sua ma-maaraŋ miana.
S.PHON: kaʔan taavaɾaʔən tumaniuɾaʔə sua karianumai nipapaʦəvərə kitana maritakarə misai sua mamaaraŋ miana
S.FORM: "ka'an taavara'en t<um>aniura'e sua karianumai nipapacevere kitana maritakare," misai sua mamaarang miana.
S.PHON: kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔen tumaniu[r|ɾ]aʔe sua ka[r|ɾ]ianumai nipapaʦeve[r|ɾ]e kitana ma[r|ɾ]itaka[r|ɾ]e misai sua mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana
S.TRANSL: "We would not abuse any pangolins because it kept us (people) alive," the elders in the past said.

S.FORM: araanai=ci=kita ʔinia ma-manu ma-ʔula sua t<in>mana=pa kari ma-maaraŋ miana ia, ma-naasə taavalaʔə kari.
S.PHON: araanaitʂikita ʔinia mamanu maʔuɾa sua tinmanapa kari mamaaraŋ miana ia manaasə taavaɾaʔə kari
S.FORM: araanaicikita 'inia mamanu ma'ura sua t<in>manapa kari mamaarang miana ia, manaase taavara'e kari.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aanaitʂikita ʔinia mamanu maʔu[r|ɾ]a sua tinmanapa ka[r|ɾ]i mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia manaase taava[r|ɾ]aʔe ka[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: In the past, we still heard the elders saying these words when we were young, so we know them.

S.FORM: nakai sua kuu=cu t<un>mana ia, kaʔan taavalaʔə masi-raru kaʔan tia=taavalaʔə. ma-naasə paa-ʔupa-ʔupaŋ=kia maamia misai.
S.PHON: nakai sua kuuʦu tunmana ia kaʔan taavaɾaʔə maʂiraru kaʔan tiataavaɾaʔə manaasə paaʔupaʔupaŋkia maamia misai
S.FORM: nakai sua kuucu t<un>mana ia, ka'an taavara'e masiraru ka'an tiataavara'e. manaase paa'upa'upangkia maamia misai.
S.PHON: nakai sua kuuʦu tunmana ia kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔe maʂi[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]u kaʔan tiataava[r|ɾ]aʔe manaase paaʔupaʔupaŋkia maamia misai
S.TRANSL: But those who didn't hear it naturally wouldn't know. We would certainly mess up pangolins.

S.FORM: kuu=cu t<un>mana kaari ma-maaraŋ miana.
S.PHON: kuuʦu tunmana kaari mamaaraŋ miana
S.FORM: kuucu t<un>mana kaari mamaarang miana.
S.PHON: kuuʦu tunmana kaa[r|ɾ]i mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana
S.TRANSL: (Younger people) have not heard the elders' words from the past.
